bib.title: Active Prompting with Chain-of-Thought for Large Language Models

read.skipped: Exemplar tables 13-18 skimmed (prompt text only); reference list skimmed

question: Which questions should be annotated with chain-of-thought rationales to make the best few-shot exemplars for a task?
hypothesis: Annotating the questions on which the LLM is most uncertain (reducing model uncertainty) yields better exemplars than fixed or random ones.
contributions: Propose to judiciously select the most helpful and informative questions for annotation, reducing the human engineering workload.
Introduce an effective uncertainty-based question selection strategy with several different uncertainty metrics.
Method surpasses competitive baselines by a large margin on multiple reasoning tasks.

method.summary: Active-Prompt: query the LLM k times per question from a pool of unlabeled training questions, score uncertainty (disagreement, entropy, variance, self-confidence), pick top-n most uncertain, have a human write CoT rationales, use them as few-shot exemplars with self-consistency at inference.
method.task: Arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning via few-shot CoT prompting

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: 1000 randomly sampled train questions for uncertainty estimation; eval on test

datasets.name: CSQA
datasets.split: eval on dev (no public test labels)

datasets.name: Letter (4)
datasets.split: OOD: prompts use two-letter names, test four

inference.decoding: Uncertainty estimation: sample k answers per question; inference: self-consistency, most consistent answer
inference.samples: 40 samples per test question for self-consistency (gpt-3.5-turbo and some rows run without SC); k = 10 samples per training question for uncertainty estimation; 1000 candidate questions; GSM8K pool resampled with seeds 1, 12, 42 (Table 7)
inference.prompting: Few-shot CoT with n exemplars as Wei et al.: 8 for GSM8K, ASDiv, SVAMP, SingleEq; 7 CSQA; 6 StrategyQA; 4 AQuA and Letter. Uncertainty-estimation stage uses Wei et al. exemplars (or zero-shot 'Let's think step by step'). Number of human-annotated questions = number of exemplars (8 for GSM8K); ASDiv/SVAMP/SingleEq reuse GSM8K annotations.

parameters.k: 10 (all main experiments; Fig 2 shows 1,5,10,15 on text-davinci-003, converges at 10)
parameters.n: number of exemplars per dataset above
parameters.tie_break: random among ties at max uncertainty; StrategyQA uses entropy / frequency for D
parameters.entropy: argmax over questions of -sum P ln P with P answer frequency
parameters.variance: answers normalized by sum of numbers in the question
parameters.self_confidence: categorical {very confident, confident, not confident, wrong answer}

other.annotator: one co-author, no trial and error; annotator B uses GSM8K gold rationales

eval.protocol: Single run per cell; CoT and SC numbers mostly copied from original papers (rest from DIVERSE); test sets same as Wei et al.; no significance tests; seed variance only for GSM8K pool sampling (Table 7)

availability.data: public datasets; full annotated exemplars in appendix Tables 13-18

prompts.text: For the question q and the predicted answer a, report the confidence about the answer from choices. (a) very confident (b) confident (c) not confident (d) wrong answer

limits: Only text-davinci-002 or -003 could be run fully (cost); no GPT-4; no self-consistency for gpt-3.5-turbo.
code-davinci-002 access shut off, making main experiments hard to reproduce.
Annotation done by one co-author; annotator choice changes results (GSM8K gold rationales beat own).
Self-confidence uncertainty fails (LLM over-confident); Llama-2 logits also overconfident.
Pool limited to 1000 training questions; ASDiv/SVAMP/SingleEq depend on transferring GSM8K exemplars, which gives smaller gains.
Diversity and complexity combination left to future work; single run, no significance tests.
